traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Proteaceae: leaves usually alternate, sometimes opposite or whorled; leaves simple or compound; compound leaves usually pinnate, sometimes palmate; margins entire, crenate, serrate or dentate; veins single, pinnate, palmate or parallel; leaves evergreen; blades linear; stipules absent; leaf rosettes basal, none or terminal; plants usually hermaphrodite, sometimes monoecious, polygamous or dioecious; ovary superior; floral cup usually present, sometimes absent; stems usually woody, sometimes herbaceous; flowers in racemes, in spikes, in heads or in umbels, sometimes solitary; flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic; perianth usually tepals, sometimes sepals and petals; fruit follicle, drupe, nut or achene; parts of each whorl 4; stamens (3-) 4; carpels 1. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Proteaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.
